candidates.buyer: Small shops, takeaways, bars and food vendors; family firms in Apia and Savai'i
candidates.existing: No vendor seen. Application forms and licences are paper-based; the trade portal at samoa.tradeportal.org lists the procedures but I did not confirm whether it takes online applications.
candidates.name: Licence-renewal compliance calendar for shops, takeaways and bars (business licence + alcohol licence + food health certificate + food handler cards)
candidates.trigger: Business Licences Act 1998 (no trading without a current licence; Register under s9). Alcohol Control Act 2020 renewal on the same cycle (2023 deadline 31 March, non-renewal means revocation). Food Act 2015 s13 health certificate attached to the licence application. Food handler health cards.
candidates.trigger_note: Per-licence renewals cluster each year, so a reminder and document-pack service is plausible but thin.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search in Samoan (e.g. software or app plus laisene pisinisi plus fa'amanuiaga) was not run because the search budget was used up. Not checked: number of licensed shops and bars, whether MCR has an online renewal portal, fee levels, and whether anyone would pay for a reminder service. Market is very small.

candidates.buyer: Bus and taxi owners (reserved to Samoan citizens under the Foreign Investment Act 2000)
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, small bus fleets
candidates.existing: None seen. Competitor search not run.
candidates.name: Bus and taxi owner fleet compliance: quarterly or twice-yearly LTA Certificate of Fitness reminders, late-fee avoidance, document pack
candidates.trigger: LTA: taxis renew March and September, commercial buses every 3 months; Certificate of Fitness plus Business Licence Certificate and commercial driver's licence; late inspection fee SAT 53 (taxi) and SAT 26.50 (bus); offence to drive a PSV with an expired certificate.
candidates.unchecked: Number of PSV operators and fleet sizes; whether LTA already sends reminders; current fee schedule; the 2018 taxi age rule. The 2019 quarterly audit report may be stale. Low value per customer.

candidates.buyer: Foreign investors, trustees and local firms with foreign shareholders; Samoan shop owners at risk of reserved-activity breaches
candidates.category: 33. Foreign Investment Act reserved activities and Amendment Bill 2026
candidates.evidence: https://samoaobserver.ws/category/samoa/121615 ; https://www.mcil.gov.ws/ (May 2024 MCIL notice reported via search: 140 of 300 shop renewals in 2023 suspected foreign-run)
candidates.name: Foreign Investment Amendment Bill 2026: registration certificate (24-month renewal) and beneficial owner disclosure tooling
candidates.trigger: Bill passed second reading in August 2026 and is with the Economic Committee, so not law. Would add certificates valid 24 months, beneficial-owner disclosure for companies and trusts, trustees reporting changes within 14 working days, fines up to 500 penalty units. Section 14 of the 2000 Act already makes reserved-activity breaches an offence.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the Bill becomes law and when; whether existing businesses must re-register; population is mostly law-firm and corporate-agent work, not quiet family firms.

candidates.buyer: Licensed fish processors and exporters, small longline operators
candidates.category: 30. Small exporters facing traceability or certification rules (also 36)
candidates.evidence: https://palemene.ws/PDFfiles/S.R. 2022-1 Fisheries Management (Fish Processing and Export) Regulations 2022 - Eng_English.pdf ; https://paclii.org/ws/legis/consol_act_2013/fa1988110
candidates.name: Fish processing and export establishment records (Fisheries Management (Fish Processing and Export) Regulations 2022)
candidates.trigger: S.R. 2022-1 processing licences for establishments and export certification; Fisheries Act 1988 Part VA, with a Samoa Seafood Standards Council.
candidates.unchecked: The Regulations text was not opened. Record and logbook duties, the number of licensed establishments, and whether MAF Fisheries runs its own system are all unknown. Likely fewer than 20 firms.

candidates.buyer: Butchers, pig and cattle slaughter operators, abattoir operators
candidates.existing: None seen; central or mobile abattoir funded by World Bank (undated report).
candidates.name: Slaughter and Meat Supply Act 2015: approved establishment records, traceability and inspection booking
candidates.trigger: Slaughter and Meat Supply Act 2015: approved establishments, record-keeping, traceability, health marking; no sale of uninspected carcasses to shops.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the Act is actually enforced for pigs and poultry; regulations, forms and list of approved establishments were not found. Very few buyers.

candidates.buyer: Small commercial exporters and the farmers they source from
candidates.category: 30. Small exporters facing traceability or certification rules; 22
candidates.existing: Applications go by email or in person to MAF Biosecurity. The PHAMA Plus manual is donor-funded guidance, not software. No private product found. Competitor search not run.
candidates.name: Export compliance pack for taro, kava, nonu and banana exporters (farm registration, per-destination export licence, phytosanitary and hot-water treatment records)
candidates.trigger: MAF Biosecurity: produce must come from a registered farm; each commercial exporter needs an export licence per destination country; treatment, inspection and phytosanitary certificates (taro to Australia and NZ, American Samoa). Temporary taro ban to American Samoa in 2018, status unknown.
candidates.unchecked: Kava and nonu export rules not found at all. Number of active exporters, whether MAF is digitising permits, and who the donor (PHAMA Plus) will hand tools to. Competitor search in local language not run because the search budget was used up.

candidates.buyer: Family-run beach fale and homestay operators
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
candidates.name: Accommodation licence and standards compliance for beach fales, homestays and guest houses
candidates.trigger: Tourism Development Act 2012: licensing of all tourism accommodation including beach fales and homestays; Samoa Tourism Authority is regulator. Matai permission also needed for fale operations.
candidates.unchecked: Licence fees, forms, inspection cycle, any guest register or levy rule, and current operator count (128 in a 2020 article). No VAGST or tourism levy duty was confirmed.

candidates.buyer: Real estate agents, lawyers and accountants acting as financial institutions
candidates.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with AML reports
candidates.name: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 compliance (customer ID, record keeping, transaction reports) for real estate agents, small law and accounting offices
candidates.trigger: MLPA 2007 (consolidated 2025); Central Bank of Samoa brochures say reporting entities must verify identity, keep records, report certain transactions and run a compliance regime; Samoa FIU receives reports.
candidates.unchecked: Schedule 1 list, reporting thresholds, the FIU's filing channel (goAML or paper) and the number of reporters. Probably under 100 entities.

candidates.existing: Free state portal businessregistries.gov.ws already emails a reminder on day 1 of the filing month and takes payment, so this is largely covered.
candidates.name: Annual return reminders and filings for family companies (Companies Act 2001)
candidates.trigger: MCIL notice 3 June 2026: file in anniversary month or risk removal after six months; restoration fee payable.
candidates.unchecked: Registry fee and whether the portal covers payment by non-card methods. Likely not worth building.

candidates.buyer: 11 licensed MTOs and money changers and their agents
candidates.category: 37. Money transfer operators and exchange control
candidates.existing: Many MTOs are branches of regional players (Fexco, KlickEx, Digicel, Vodafone) with their own systems.
candidates.name: Money transfer operator and money-changer agent compliance (Central Bank of Samoa exchange control, delegated approval limits)
candidates.trigger: Exchange Control Information Booklet 2026; dealers licensed by the Central Bank; delegated approval limits from 1 August 2023; AML duties under the MLPA.
candidates.unchecked: Sub-agent licensing, reporting forms and frequency. Buyers are few and mostly large foreign-owned.

candidates.buyer: Private recruiters and employer companies in the seasonal worker schemes
candidates.existing: MCIL states it holds the exclusive right to administer all activities under the NZ and Australian schemes; LEEP registration is free and runs the national recruitment database. Cabinet approves every worker's departure.
candidates.name: Private recruiter registration and candidate uploads for RSE and PALM schemes
candidates.trigger: Savali notice (Sept 2023): recruiters need an office and must upload all candidate data to the LEEP In-Country Recruitment Database.
candidates.unchecked: Whether private recruiters still operate after the 2023 and later policy changes (an older report says oversight moved to the Ministry of Finance).

candidates.existing: 7+ accredited vendors already listed in K02.
candidates.known_note: Same duty and buyer as K01 and K02. The April 2026 notice of enforcement with penalties and no more extensions is new evidence on demand, but it does not remove the vendor crowd that killed K02. A fresh vendor check for a K02 revive was not run.
candidates.name: TIMS reconciliation and POS for VAGST businesses
candidates.trigger: Ministry notice 1 April 2026: refresher training 30 April to 7 May 2026, no more extensions, penalties will start.

candidates.name: Plumbers Act 2014 annual registration renewals
candidates.trigger: Annual renewal of certificate of registration; offence to plumb unregistered.
candidates.unchecked: Number of plumbers; likely only dozens. Not worth building.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). Only generic SNPF (employer and employee 7% each, due the 14th of the following month, per third-party payroll guide) and monthly PAYE P4 filing appear; generic payroll is out of scope.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Microstate with very few dealers; no regime found incidentally.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Nothing came up incidentally.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No gold trade of note in Samoa; any AML duty would fall under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 Schedule 1, which was not checked.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Nothing found incidentally.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Slaughter and Meat Supply Act 2015 (approved establishments, record-keeping and traceability, health marking), enforced by the MAF veterinary service. Initially beef; whether it now covers pigs and poultry is unverified. Few operators. Candidate C5.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Slaughter and Meat Supply Act 2015: carcasses cannot go to shops unless inspected. A central or mobile abattoir was planned with World Bank money (undated). Tiny number of approved establishments. Candidate C5.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Not searched (budget).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Only the MAF veterinary service as Competent Authority was found. No private vet licensing regime was found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Not searched (budget).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Samoa Water Authority (Sewerage and Wastewater) Regulations 2009 cover trade-waste discharge permits and septic tanks being made inoperable once a property connects to a public sewer. No desludging licence found. Plumbers Act 2014 requires registration and annual renewal of plumbers; the register is tiny. Nothing worth building.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Microstate with few lifts.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Not searched. Samoa Water Authority is the dominant provider.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Not searched (budget).

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: MCIL says it holds the exclusive right to administer the NZ RSE and Australian PALM schemes. The LEEP in-country recruitment database is free. Private recruiters must upload candidate data to LEEP (Savali notice, Sept 2023). Candidate C11, rejected.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Burial is mostly family and village land.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: One search on the MJCA charities and societies register returned only Fiji and NZ material. No Samoa-specific duty was confirmed. Marked unverified; no candidate.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: LTA requires taxis to renew twice a year (March and September) and commercial buses four times a year, with a Certificate of Fitness. The applicant must bring a valid Business Licence Certificate and a commercial licence. Late fees are SAT 53 for taxis and SAT 26.50 for buses. Public bus and taxi services are reserved for Samoan citizens under the Foreign Investment Act. Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Food vendors need a health card and Ministry clearance (SAT 10). Money changers and money transfer operators are licensed by the Central Bank of Samoa; 11 named in the 2026 Exchange Control Booklet. Candidates C1 and C10.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Food businesses need a Food Act 2015 health certificate, attached to the business licence application. Early childhood centre licensing could not be confirmed. No Samoan tattoo or driving school regime found. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Retail fuel prices are set monthly by the Ministry of Finance. No distributor or station licensing regime was found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: The main commodity exports are taro, nonu, kava and coconut products. MAF requires a registered farm source and a per-destination export licence, plus phytosanitary certificates and hot-water treatment for Australia. Candidate C6.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Not searched (budget).

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Pharmacy Act 2007 covers pharmacists and pharmacy supervision. No private clinic registration scheme and no insurer billing regime found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacy Act 2007 and the Pharmacists Council (annual practising certificates). Only a handful of pharmacies. No premises or controlled-drug register found in snippets. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Only the RSE and PALM recruiter regime was seen, under category 15.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: PUMA development consent is required for any structure. No general builder licence found; only plumbers are registered. The National Building Code is a 2017 draft and its adoption is unconfirmed. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (consolidated 2025). The Central Bank of Samoa and the Samoa FIU publish guides for lawyers, accountants and real estate agents covering customer identification, record keeping, transaction reporting and a compliance regime. Small population of reporters. Candidate C8.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism Development Act 2012 licenses all accommodation, including beach fales and homestays; the Samoa Tourism Authority is the regulator. About 128 properties as of 2020. No guest register or levy rule found. Candidate C7.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: MAF Biosecurity export licence per destination, registered farm sourcing and phytosanitary certification. Fisheries Management (Fish Processing and Export) Regulations 2022 cover processing licences and export certification. Candidates C4 and C6.

coverage.category: 31. Alcohol licensing (Alcohol Control Act 2020, Alcohol Control Board)
coverage.found: The Act commenced 1 July 2021 and replaced the Liquor Act 2011. Licences are renewed annually on the business licence cycle; in 2023 the deadline was extended to 31 March and non-renewal meant revocation. Applications are paper forms from the Liquor Board secretary. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 32. Food Act 2015 health certificates and food handler cards
coverage.found: Health certificate from the Director General of Health, issued by the Food Safety Office at Motootua, and required before a food business licence. Food handlers need a health card (SAT 10), training and medical screening. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 33. Foreign Investment Act 2000 reserved activities and the Foreign Investment Amendment Bill 2026
coverage.found: The Bill passed second reading in August 2026 and went to the Economic Committee; it is not law yet. It would add a registration certificate (24 months, renewable) and beneficial owner disclosure, with trustees reporting changes within 14 working days. In 2023, 140 of 300 shop renewals were suspected of being foreign-run. Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 34. Business Licences Act 1998 annual renewals and the Register of Business Licences (Ministry of Customs and Revenue)
coverage.found: No one may carry on business without a current licence; the Register is kept under section 9. Renewal now includes beneficial-owner checks. Renewal is a precondition for the LTA, alcohol and food licences. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 35. Tobacco Control Act 2008 and Licensing Regulations 2020
coverage.found: Licences apply to manufacturers, importers, distributors, hotel owners and nightclub owners only; no shop licence found. Very few licensees. Nothing worth building.

coverage.category: 36. Fisheries and Shipping Acts: vessel licensing, fish processing and export
coverage.found: Fisheries Act 1988 (local commercial vessel licensing, Part VA processing and marketing), the 2022 Processing and Export Regulations, and Shipping Act 1998 vessel registration. Exempt-vessel list and small-boat rules not read. Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 37. Money transfer operators and exchange control (Central Bank of Samoa)
coverage.found: 11 licensed MTOs and money changers in the 2026 Exchange Control Booklet, with delegated approval limits (SAT 50,000 for local investment transfers from August 2023). MTOs handle about 80% of remittance inflows. Candidate C10.

coverage.category: 38. Companies Act 2001 annual returns (Registry of Companies, MCIL)
coverage.found: MCIL notice of 3 June 2026: every company files an annual return in its anniversary month, and non-filers can be removed after six months. The portal at businessregistries.gov.ws emails reminders and has no financial statements requirement. Candidate C9.

coverage.category: 39. TIMS fiscal invoicing for VAGST-registered businesses
coverage.found: Ministry notice of 1 April 2026: mandatory refresher training 30 April to 7 May 2026, no more extensions, penalties to begin. Already known as K01 and K02.
